title: Tighten WebView UI cohesion labels
summary: Tightens WebView operator-workstation terminology, queue loaded-row priority scope copy, rename filter staging, shared status labels, and low-risk accessibility contracts without changing backend route ownership or media policy.
reason: The UI cohesion review found labels and controls that could imply filtered WebView evidence changed backend scope or that rename filter draft storage persisted settings. This pass clarifies backend-owned mutation boundaries and pins canonical labels in source and tests.
behavior_before: Queue movie/TV bulk priority copy used generic All Movies/All TV wording and visible-row language. Rename filter save behaved like a direct settings save path. Raw pending status could map ambiguously, passive status chips entered tab order, the active nav lacked aria-current, and sparkline metadata conflicted with decorative aria-hidden use.
behavior_after: Queue loaded-row bulk priority uses All Loaded Movies/All Loaded TV, confirms loaded and filtered counts before posting, and states Launch scope remains backend-owned. Rename filters stage persisted keys into Settings Changes JSON for normal Preview Patch and Save Settings. Shared status helpers split queue pending, parked, drain pending, publishing, failed, and unknown states. Passive chips are not tabbable, active nav exposes aria-current, and the sparkline is decorative only.
